title: Fork Dracula theme and create Neon Dracula full theme
description:
Convert the neon-dracula CSS snippet into a full Obsidian theme by forking the Dracula theme repo and merging our neon effects.

## Background
We created a CSS snippet at ~/workspace/obsidian-neon-dracula/neon-dracula.css that adds neon cyberpunk effects to Obsidian's Dracula theme. The snippet is already pushed to https://github.com/scbrown/obsidian-neon-dracula

To publish to the Obsidian community themes marketplace, we need to convert it from a snippet (that layers on Dracula) to a standalone full theme.

## Current Snippet Features (neon-dracula.css)
- **Headers**: Golden orange (#ffcc66) with neon glow + black text outline for readability
- **Inline code**: Neon green (#50fa7b) with glow, dark background (#44475a)
- **Tables**: Purple borders (#bd93f9) with neon glow, alternating row colors, pink accent on header (#ff79c6)
- **Code blocks**: Purple borders (#bd93f9), glow in reading mode only (live preview has per-line div limitation)
- **Comments in code**: Cyan (#8be9fd) italic with subtle glow
- **Tags, italics, list bullets**: Neon green
- **Links**: Orange with glow
- **Bold**: Orange with glow
- **Blockquotes**: Green left border with glow

## Font Configuration (ADD THIS)
Use Intel One Mono as primary font with fallbacks:
```css
body {
  --font-text: 'Intel One Mono', 'Fira Code', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
  --font-monospace: 'Intel One Mono', 'Fira Code', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
  --font-interface: 'Intel One Mono', 'Fira Code', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
}
```

## Steps to Complete
1. Fork https://github.com/dracula/obsidian to scbrown/neon-dracula-obsidian (or similar)
2. Merge neon-dracula.css effects into the forked theme's obsidian.css
3. Add the font configuration with fallbacks
4. Create/update manifest.json:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "Neon Dracula",
     "version": "1.0.0",
     "minAppVersion": "1.0.0",
     "author": "scbrown",
     "authorUrl": "https://github.com/scbrown"
   }
   ```
5. Rename main CSS file to theme.css (Obsidian requirement)
6. Take screenshot.png of the theme in action
7. Submit PR to https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-releases adding entry to community-css-themes.json:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "Neon Dracula",
     "author": "scbrown",
     "repo": "scbrown/neon-dracula-obsidian",
     "screenshot": "screenshot.png",
     "modes": ["dark"]
   }
   ```

## Key Colors (Dracula palette)
- Orange: #ffb86c (dracula), #ffcc66 (our brighter version), #ffa54f (medium)
- Green: #50fa7b
- Purple: #bd93f9
- Cyan: #8be9fd
- Pink: #ff79c6
- Background: #282a36
- Current line: #44475a
- Comment: #6272a4

## Known Limitation
Code block glow only works in reading mode. In live preview/edit mode, Obsidian renders each line as a separate div, causing glow artifacts. We use clean borders without glow for edit mode.
